prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: دورات تدريبية معتمدة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "اسم الدورة" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 250px
  col 2: header "المدة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 168px
  col 3: header "المدرب" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 105px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 1420px
  col 5: header "الرسوم" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 70px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1A: widths [190, 90, 95, 275, 69] · table 720×906px · row heights [36, 176, 129, 129, 129, 153, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [210, 88, 95, 257, 69] · table 720×952px · row heights [36, 176, 153, 129, 153, 153, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [190, 82, 84, 272, 91] · table 720×906px · row heights [36, 176, 129, 129, 129, 153, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [170, 82, 86, 290, 91] · table 720×836px · row heights [36, 153, 129, 129, 129, 129, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [205, 80, 85, 258, 91] · table 720×952px · row heights [36, 176, 153, 129, 153, 153, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [180, 78, 78, 292, 91] · table 720×813px · row heights [36, 153, 129, 106, 129, 129, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [172, 76, 80, 300, 91] · table 720×813px · row heights [36, 153, 129, 106, 129, 129, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [190, 76, 82, 280, 91] · table 720×859px · row heights [36, 176, 129, 129, 129, 129, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r3A"],"acceptable":["r2B","r3B","r3C","r2A","r2C","r1A"],"bad":[{"design":"r1B","why":"The description is squeezed to 257px while the course-name column is given 210px, producing the tallest table (952px) and a cramped reading column; the 69px fee column also splits the amount from the currency, so a semantic unit breaks across lines."}],"contrast":null,"ranges":[[176,190],[76,88],[76,90],[292,300],[91,98]],"rationale":"In this RTL course catalogue the eye enters at the course name on the right, then reads the description, with duration, trainer and fee as supporting facts. r3A gives the description the dominant share (292px) while keeping the course-name row header wide enough to avoid most unnecessary label breaks, and it keeps the fee column at 91px so “1.850 ر.س” stays on one line. The narrower duration and trainer columns wrap their short contents, but row height is driven by the description, so those wraps cost no vertical space; the result is the shortest table (813px) with no mid-word splits and no wrapped headers.","principles":{"general":["Allocate width by reading and comparison role, not by symmetry: narrative or descriptive columns usually deserve the largest share, while short numeric or currency columns need just enough width to keep units intact.","The row-header column must stay scannable but should not rival the main body column; if it becomes too wide, it steals lines from the content that sets row height.","Widen the column that determines row height until it reduces line count; adding width to short secondary columns often adds no compactness.","Keep semantic units such as amount plus currency together even when no word is split mid-character."],"specific":["This is an Arabic RTL course table: the course name is the rightmost row header, the description is the body, and duration/trainer/fee are secondary attributes.","At 15px, the fee column needs about 91px to keep “ر.س” beside the amount; 69px forces a two-line fee cell.","A description width around 292px lets the third row drop to fewer lines, which is why r3A reaches 813px while similar designs with 280–290px descriptions grow taller.","Duration and trainer can be as narrow as 76–78px here because their cells are shorter than the description and therefore do not determine row height."]},"tradeoffs":"The main disagreement is how much width the course-name row header deserves versus the description. A designer prioritizing maximum description measure might choose the 172/300 split of r3B; I chose 180/292 because it keeps more course labels intact without increasing table height. Another tradeoff is accepting wrapped duration/trainer cells in exchange for a wider description, which works here because those cells are not the tallest.","uncertain":"Whether a two-line fee cell is a genuine publication fault or merely a minor compromise; whether r3A and r3B are effectively equal given browser text rounding; and the exact description-width threshold where a line drops may shift slightly with font rendering."}
